route: Stripe hires for judgement under ambiguity more than for raw puzzle speed. The interviews are deliberately practical: you write real code in a real editor against a real repository, and you are graded on how you get unstuck as much as on whether you finish.

stages.name: Application review
stages.detail: A recruiter reads the CV against the specific team. A referral or a public project moves this along materially.

stages.name: Recruiter screen
stages.detail: Thirty minutes on motivation, level and compensation range. Come with a number.

stages.name: Technical phone screen
stages.detail: One practical coding problem in a shared editor, in your own language, with tests you are expected to run.

stages.name: Onsite loop
stages.detail: Integration coding, debugging an unfamiliar codebase, system design, and a values interview.

stages.name: Team match and offer
stages.detail: Hiring manager conversations, then a written offer with the band.

focus.topic: Practical coding in a real repo
focus.note: No whiteboards. Bring a language you can debug in without help.
Design an idempotent endpoint and defend the schema behind it.
You will be dropped into a codebase and asked to fix it.
Present, but rarely the deciding factor.

signals: A shipped side project with users, not a tutorial clone
Written communication — Stripe runs on documents
Evidence you have handled money, correctness or compliance before

openings.name: Stripe Engineering Internship, Summer
openings.detail: Twelve weeks, paid, with a named mentor and a project that ships. Historically converts to full-time at a high rate.

openings.name: Online technical assessment
openings.window: Sent within a week of application review
openings.detail: Two practical problems, roughly 90 minutes, run in a browser IDE with tests.

openings.name: Stripe Fellowship for early-career engineers
openings.detail: A paid apprenticeship route into a full-time engineering role.

prepare.label: Build one thing end to end
prepare.detail: A small payments or billing app with webhooks, retries and idempotency. This is the exact vocabulary of the interview.

prepare.label: Practise in your editor, not a whiteboard
prepare.detail: Time yourself solving problems with real tests and a debugger, since that is the format.

prepare.label: Write a design doc
prepare.detail: One page on a system you built: the decision, the alternatives, the trade-off. Bring it.

prepare.label: Know your number
prepare.detail: Research the band for your level and location before the recruiter screen.

route: The hardest bar on this list. Interviews weight depth over breadth: they would rather see one area you know unusually well than five you know adequately. Research-adjacent roles expect you to have read the literature and, ideally, reproduced some of it.

stages.name: Application review
stages.detail: Publications, open source and demonstrable systems work carry more weight than the CV format.

stages.name: Recruiter screen
stages.detail: Role fit, level calibration and timeline.

stages.name: Technical screen
stages.detail: Coding, plus a domain conversation matched to the role — inference, training or product infrastructure.

stages.name: Onsite loop
stages.detail: Multiple deep technical rounds, a systems design round at large scale, and a practical take-home or pairing session.

stages.name: Team match and offer
stages.detail: Matching to a specific team, then offer.

focus.note: Distributed training, inference optimisation or large-scale serving. Pick one and go far.
GPU scheduling, batching, caching, queueing. Real numbers expected.
Read the paper, implement the paper, explain what the paper got wrong.
Not scripts — services that stay up.

signals: A reproduction of a published result, with your write-up of what differed
Open source contributions to a serving or training framework
Evidence you have run something large and had it break

openings.name: Residency and internship programmes
openings.window: Applications typically open in the autumn
openings.eligibility: Graduate students, and career changers with strong technical backgrounds
openings.detail: A six-month residency aimed at people moving into AI from an adjacent technical field.

openings.name: Take-home technical exercise
openings.detail: A scoped multi-hour exercise, usually profiling or optimising a piece of real inference code.

prepare.label: Pick one depth area and go three levels down
prepare.detail: Breadth loses here. Choose inference, training or data infrastructure and know it better than the interviewer expects.

prepare.label: Reproduce a paper
prepare.detail: Even partially. Write up what did not replicate — that write-up is the strongest artefact you can bring.

prepare.label: Get comfortable with very large numbers
prepare.detail: Practise estimating throughput, memory and cost out loud. Design rounds are quantitative.

prepare.label: Contribute upstream
prepare.detail: A merged PR to a serving or training framework is a direct, verifiable signal.

route: A very small team, so every hire is visible. Linear hires on taste and speed: they want to see that you notice the details other people ship past. The work-sample stage matters far more than the conversation stages.

stages.name: Application review
stages.detail: Read carefully by a human. A portfolio or repo that shows craft beats a long CV.

stages.name: Intro call
stages.detail: A conversation with a founder or team lead about what you care about in software.

stages.name: Work sample
stages.detail: A paid, scoped project close to the real work. This is the main gate.

stages.name: Team conversations
stages.detail: Two or three sessions reviewing the work sample and how you think.

stages.name: Offer
stages.detail: Fast decisions once the loop finishes.

focus.note: Alignment, motion, empty states, keyboard paths. They will notice.
Prototype fast, iterate faster, do not gold-plate the wrong thing.
Be able to explain what you chose not to build.
Sub-100ms is a stated product value, not a stretch goal.

signals: A portfolio piece where you can articulate every decision
Something you built that is genuinely fast
Strong opinions about tools you actually use daily

openings.name: Work-sample hiring for all roles
openings.eligibility: All candidates who pass the intro call
openings.detail: Paid project work instead of a traditional interview loop. Expect to be compensated for your time.

prepare.label: Ship something small and perfect
prepare.detail: One tool, finished to a standard you would defend publicly. Scope down until you can make it excellent.

prepare.label: Learn the keyboard-first idiom
prepare.detail: Use the product. Understand why it is built the way it is before you critique it.

prepare.label: Prepare to defend a decision
prepare.detail: For every portfolio piece, know the alternative you rejected and why.

prepare.label: Measure your own work
prepare.detail: Bring a number — load time, frame budget, bundle size. It signals you take performance seriously.

route: Figma runs one of the more rigorous design loops in the industry and an engineering loop that leans heavily on real-world debugging. Designers should expect a portfolio review with hard questions; engineers should expect graphics, performance or systems depth.

stages.name: Application review
stages.detail: Portfolio for design, repositories and experience for engineering.

stages.name: Recruiter screen
stages.detail: Role, level and logistics.

stages.name: Portfolio or technical screen
stages.detail: Designers present two projects in depth. Engineers do a practical coding round.

stages.name: Onsite loop
stages.detail: Craft round, collaboration round, systems or architecture round, and a values interview.

stages.name: Debrief and offer
stages.detail: Panel debrief, then offer.

focus.note: Two projects, told properly: problem, constraint, iteration, outcome.
Canvas, WebGL, WebAssembly. Multiplayer is a rendering problem.
Components are APIs. Talk about them that way.
Explicitly assessed in its own round.

signals: Work that shows iteration, including the versions that failed
Experience with real-time or collaborative interfaces
Ability to critique your own work before someone else does

openings.name: Figma Design and Engineering Internship
openings.window: Applications typically open in the autumn for the following summer
openings.detail: Twelve weeks on a product team with a mentor and a real shipping project.

openings.name: Config student and early-career track
openings.detail: Portfolio reviews and recruiting sessions run alongside the company's annual conference.

openings.name: Take-home design exercise
openings.detail: A scoped product problem with a written rationale, reviewed in a later round.

prepare.label: Cut your portfolio to two projects
prepare.detail: Depth beats breadth every time in this loop. Twenty minutes each, rehearsed.

prepare.label: Prepare the failure story
prepare.detail: Every craft round asks what went wrong. Have a real answer with what you changed.

prepare.label: Engineers: build something on canvas
prepare.detail: Even a small collaborative drawing tool teaches the exact problems they ask about.

prepare.label: Use the product seriously
prepare.detail: Enough to have informed opinions about its edges.

route: Remote-first since long before it was common, so the process is asynchronous and writing-heavy. Your public GitHub profile is genuinely read. Expect a take-home rather than a live algorithm round for most engineering positions.

stages.name: Application review
stages.detail: Your profile and contribution history are part of the application whether you link them or not.

stages.name: Recruiter screen
stages.detail: Role, remote logistics and level.

stages.name: Take-home exercise
stages.detail: A scoped project done on your own time, with a written explanation of your choices.

stages.name: Panel interviews
stages.detail: Technical review of your take-home, a systems round and a collaboration round, all remote.

stages.name: Offer
stages.detail: Offer with location-adjusted band.

focus.note: A distributed company decides in writing. Your take-home write-up is assessed.
Know more than the porcelain commands.
Everything here has a very large number in front of it.
Code review etiquette and issue triage are real skills here.

signals: A public contribution history with thoughtful pull request descriptions
Documentation you have written
Evidence of working well asynchronously across time zones

openings.name: GitHub Internship Programme
openings.window: Applications typically open in the autumn
openings.detail: Fully remote internship with a mentor, running twelve weeks over the summer.

openings.name: GitHub Campus Expert
openings.eligibility: Students running technical communities at their institution
openings.detail: Training and support for student community leaders. A well-trodden route into the internship programme.

openings.name: Take-home engineering exercise
openings.detail: A scoped repository task with a required written rationale.

prepare.label: Tidy your public profile
prepare.detail: It is read. Pin the repositories that show your best judgement, not your most stars.

prepare.label: Practise writing about code
prepare.detail: Write a README for something you built that explains the decisions, not just the setup.

prepare.label: Learn Git below the surface
prepare.detail: Objects, refs, packfiles, rebase mechanics. It comes up.

prepare.label: Contribute to one project properly
prepare.detail: One well-reviewed contribution beats twenty drive-by commits.

route: A fast, relatively short loop with a strong bias toward people who are already visible in the frontend community. Building in public is close to a shortcut here — a widely used open source project or a well-known talk will get your application read.

stages.name: Application review
stages.detail: Public work counts heavily. A popular package or a good technical blog is a real advantage.

stages.name: Recruiter screen
stages.detail: Fit and level.

stages.name: Technical screen
stages.detail: Practical frontend or infrastructure problem, live.

stages.name: Team loop
stages.detail: System design, a product sense round and a manager conversation.

stages.name: Offer
stages.detail: Decisions move quickly once the loop is done.

focus.note: Rendering, hydration, caching, bundling. Framework-level understanding.
Why an API feels good is a real interview topic here.
Know what is cached where, and what invalidates it.
Writing and speaking are part of many roles.

signals: An open source package other people depend on
A conference talk or a technical blog with real depth
Strong opinions about framework trade-offs, held loosely

openings.name: Vercel Summer Internship
openings.window: Applications typically open early in the year
openings.detail: A remote internship with one scoped project shipped to production.

openings.name: Open source contributor path
openings.detail: Sustained contributions to the framework repositories are a recognised and well-used route into a role.

prepare.label: Publish something people use
prepare.detail: A small, genuinely useful package with good docs is the highest-leverage thing you can do here.

prepare.label: Learn the rendering model properly
prepare.detail: Streaming, hydration, caching layers. Be able to draw the request path on a whiteboard.

prepare.label: Write one good technical post
prepare.detail: Explain something hard clearly. It doubles as your communication assessment.

prepare.label: Contribute upstream
prepare.detail: A merged PR to the core repositories puts your name in front of the team before you apply.

route: A traditional, well-structured loop with unusually deep networking and systems questions. Cloudflare hires globally and runs consistent processes across offices, so preparation transfers well between locations.

stages.name: Application review
stages.detail: Systems experience and language depth matter more than brand names.

stages.name: Recruiter screen
stages.detail: Role, location and visa logistics.

stages.name: Technical screen
stages.detail: Coding plus fundamentals — networking, concurrency, memory.

stages.name: Onsite loop
stages.detail: Two coding rounds, a systems design round and a behavioural round.

stages.name: Offer
stages.detail: Panel review, then offer.

focus.note: TCP, TLS, DNS, HTTP. Genuinely deep questions, not trivia.
Rust, Go or C++ with real memory and concurrency understanding.
Global consistency, failure domains, progressive rollout.
Standard rounds, moderate difficulty.

signals: Something you have written that speaks a protocol directly
Experience operating a service under real traffic
Understanding of blast radius and safe deployment

openings.name: Cloudflare Internship Programme
openings.eligibility: Students in penultimate or final year, multiple global offices
openings.detail: Twelve-week internships across engineering, security and product, in several offices worldwide.

openings.name: Online coding assessment
openings.detail: A timed online assessment, typically two problems in 90 minutes, before the human screen.

openings.name: Project Alexandria and community programmes
openings.detail: Community programmes that put you in contact with the teams; not a hiring route in themselves, but useful exposure.

prepare.label: Build a protocol from scratch
prepare.detail: A minimal HTTP server or DNS resolver, written by hand. It answers half the interview.

prepare.label: Read the RFCs you claim to know
prepare.detail: Interviewers here go deeper on networking than most companies do.

prepare.label: Practise timed online assessments
prepare.detail: The first gate is automated and time-boxed. Speed matters at that stage only.

prepare.label: Learn one systems language properly
prepare.detail: Rust or Go, to the point where you understand its memory model.

route: A structured, quantitative loop. Datadog is unusually explicit about wanting people who can reason about very large data volumes, and the design rounds are correspondingly numeric — expect to estimate cardinality, storage and query cost out loud.

stages.name: Application review
stages.detail: Backend and data infrastructure experience weighted heavily.

stages.name: Recruiter screen
stages.detail: Level, location and compensation.

stages.name: Technical screen
stages.detail: Live coding, usually data-structure heavy with a practical framing.

stages.name: Onsite loop
stages.detail: Coding, a systems design round on data at scale, and a manager round.

stages.name: Offer
stages.detail: Offer with equity and stock purchase details.

focus.note: Sketches, sampling, probabilistic counting. Know the trade-offs.
Compression, retention, downsampling, cardinality explosions.
Predicate pushdown and aggregation strategies.
Profiling ability is explicitly valued.

signals: Experience with a storage or query engine, even a small one
Comfort estimating with real numbers under questioning
Operational experience — you have been paged

openings.name: Datadog Engineering Internship
openings.eligibility: Students, multiple offices including New York and Paris
openings.detail: Twelve to sixteen weeks on a product or infrastructure team, with a high conversion rate to full-time.

openings.name: Online technical assessment
openings.window: Early in the process for university hiring
openings.detail: A timed algorithmic assessment used as the first filter for campus hiring.

prepare.label: Learn probabilistic data structures
prepare.detail: HyperLogLog, count-min sketch, bloom filters. They appear in both coding and design rounds.

prepare.label: Practise numeric design out loud
prepare.detail: Estimate ingest volume, storage cost and query latency. Say the numbers.

prepare.label: Profile something real
prepare.detail: Take a slow program, profile it, make it fast, and be able to narrate what you found.

prepare.label: Understand cardinality
prepare.detail: Why high-cardinality tags break observability systems is close to a required answer here.

route: Notion weights product sense unusually highly, including for engineering roles. Nearly every loop includes a round about the product itself, and candidates who have not used it seriously tend not to get through.

stages.name: Application review
stages.detail: Product-minded experience stands out more than pure technical depth.

stages.name: Recruiter screen
stages.detail: Motivation and level.

stages.name: Technical or craft screen
stages.detail: Coding for engineers, portfolio for designers, a product exercise for product roles.

stages.name: Onsite loop
stages.detail: Two technical rounds, a product sense round and a collaboration round.

stages.name: Offer
stages.detail: Debrief, then offer.

focus.note: Assessed for engineers too. Have opinions about the product's real weaknesses.
Rich text editing at scale is genuinely hard. Know why.
CRDTs, operational transforms and the trade-offs between them.
Standard, with a bias toward document and permission models.

signals: Deep, specific criticism of the product delivered constructively
Something you built with a rich text or collaborative surface
Evidence of caring about the flexibility-versus-simplicity trade-off

openings.name: Notion Internship
openings.window: Applications typically open in the autumn
openings.detail: Twelve weeks in San Francisco or New York on a product team.

openings.name: Notion Campus Leaders
openings.detail: A student ambassador programme that builds a relationship with the recruiting team early.

prepare.label: Use the product for something real
prepare.detail: Run an actual project in it for a month. Superficial familiarity shows immediately.

prepare.label: Write a product critique
prepare.detail: Three things you would change and why, with the trade-off each would cost. Bring it.

prepare.label: Build a small collaborative editor
prepare.detail: Even a rough one teaches you the sync problems they ask about.

prepare.label: Prepare for the product round
prepare.detail: Engineers get this round too. Practise reasoning about users out loud.

route: The fastest loop of any company on this list — Ramp is explicit about speed as a competitive advantage in hiring. Expect a compressed process, often finishing within two weeks, with a strong emphasis on ownership and past velocity.

stages.name: Application review
stages.detail: Reviewed quickly. Evidence of shipping fast is the strongest signal.

stages.name: Recruiter screen
stages.detail: Level and speed of your availability.

stages.name: Technical screen
stages.detail: Practical coding, often on a realistic financial data problem.

stages.name: Onsite loop
stages.detail: System design, a practical build round, and a round on ownership and past impact.

stages.name: Offer
stages.detail: Often same-week decisions.

focus.note: Be ready to quantify what you shipped and how fast.
Idempotency, isolation levels, reconciliation. The domain demands it.
Practical, service-level design rather than abstract puzzles.
Not required, but double-entry basics help a lot.

signals: A track record of owning something end to end, alone
Numbers attached to your past work
Comfort with a fast, high-expectation environment

openings.name: Ramp Engineering Internship
openings.window: Applications typically open in the autumn
openings.eligibility: Students in penultimate year, New York and remote
openings.detail: A summer internship on a product team with real production ownership.

openings.name: Practical take-home
openings.window: Occasionally used in place of a live screen
openings.detail: A short, realistic build task rather than an algorithmic puzzle.

prepare.label: Learn double-entry bookkeeping
prepare.detail: An afternoon of reading. It makes the entire domain conversation easier.

prepare.label: Quantify your past work
prepare.detail: Every ownership question here wants a number. Prepare three stories with metrics.

prepare.label: Practise building fast
prepare.detail: Time-boxed builds — four hours, working product. That is the actual skill being tested.

prepare.label: Be available
prepare.detail: The loop moves in days, not weeks. Clear your calendar before you apply.

route: Retool interviews are unusually literal: you will build something close to what the job involves. Less algorithmic theory, more can-you-actually-build-this. Good for strong practical engineers who interview badly on puzzles.

stages.name: Application review
stages.detail: Practical building experience over credentials.

stages.name: Recruiter screen
stages.detail: Fit, level and location expectations.

stages.name: Practical screen
stages.detail: Build a small working feature, live, with internet access allowed.

stages.name: Onsite loop
stages.detail: An extended build round, a design round and a customer-empathy round.

stages.name: Offer
stages.detail: Straightforward offer process.

focus.note: The main assessment. Bring your real workflow.
Customers are engineers; you debug their apps, not yours.
Everything in the product touches a database.
A dedicated round. Technical customers, technical answers.

signals: Internal tools you have built for a real team
Evidence you can debug someone else's code calmly
A pragmatic streak — shipped beats elegant here

openings.name: Retool Internship
openings.window: Applications typically open in the autumn
openings.eligibility: Students, San Francisco and New York
openings.detail: A summer internship shipping real features, with in-office expectations.

openings.name: Support-to-engineering path
openings.detail: A recognised internal route from support engineering into product engineering.

prepare.label: Build an internal tool for someone real
prepare.detail: A dashboard or admin panel a person actually uses. That is the job.

prepare.label: Get fast in your own environment
prepare.detail: The build rounds allow your tools. Know your shortcuts and your debugger.

prepare.label: Sharpen your SQL
prepare.detail: Joins, window functions, query plans. It comes up in nearly every round.

prepare.label: Practise explaining a fix
prepare.detail: The support-adjacent round wants clarity, not jargon.

route: The most open route on this list. Supabase hires visibly from its own contributor community, and a strong history of merged pull requests can substitute for a conventional CV entirely. Everything is remote and asynchronous.

stages.name: Application review
stages.detail: Contribution history is read first. A good PR record is the application.

stages.name: Intro call
stages.detail: Async-friendly conversation about what you have built and want to build.

stages.name: Paid trial project
stages.detail: A scoped piece of real work, done in the open, paid.

stages.name: Team conversations
stages.detail: A couple of calls across time zones with the people you would work with.

stages.name: Offer
stages.detail: Remote offer with equity.

focus.note: Row level security, replication, extensions, query planning.
Public PRs, public discussion, public mistakes.
A fully distributed team across many time zones.
Small team, very little management overhead.

signals: Merged pull requests to the repositories, ideally non-trivial ones
A project you built on the platform and wrote about
Evidence you can work without daily supervision

openings.name: Contributor to hire
openings.detail: The most reliable route in. Sustained open source contribution is treated as a direct hiring signal.

openings.name: Launch Week community events
openings.detail: Public build events with hackathons; strong entries get noticed by the team directly.

openings.name: Paid trial project
openings.detail: A real, scoped, paid piece of work instead of a whiteboard loop.

prepare.label: Contribute before you apply
prepare.detail: Two or three merged pull requests change the conversation completely.

prepare.label: Learn Postgres beyond queries
prepare.detail: Row level security and replication are the areas that come up most.

prepare.label: Build and publish on the platform
prepare.detail: Ship something using it, then write up what was hard.

prepare.label: Practise writing well async
prepare.detail: Most of the assessment is how you communicate in issues and pull requests.
